name: topopt
description: Describe a part in words. Claude builds the problem, runs a topology optimization on your computer, and gives you a printable STL.
long_description:
topopt makes a part lighter. You give it the space, the mounting and the loads. It removes the material that does little work and writes a printable STL. Everything runs on your computer.

The extension gives Claude tools to build a problem from a description, check it, run it, show the dashboard link and read the result. It also gives five role playbooks (lead design, CAD, FEA, print, finish) as the tool `team_guide`, as prompts and as resources.

Target: a Mac with Apple silicon. The first start downloads Python 3.13 and about 200 MB of packages, so it takes 1 to 3 minutes. topopt connects at once with all its tools: until the setup is done, a tool call gives the setup status, and then the tools work in the same chat. The Mac needs no Python and no uv: the extension downloads a checked uv release when there is none. If the tools are missing, turn the extension off and on in Settings > Extensions; each start continues from the uv cache, so a stopped download is not lost. Runs, STLs and results go in the work folder: the folder Documents/topopt in your home folder, or the folder that you choose in the settings of the extension.

workspace.title: Work folder
workspace.description: Runs, STL files and results go in this folder (in its subfolder runs/). Relative paths in tool calls start here. When this is empty, the folder Documents/topopt in your home folder is used. After a change, quit Claude completely and open it again.

io.github.chartergroup.topopt.note: The manifest schema has no field for the CPU architecture. Apple silicon is the target on macOS. An Intel Mac (darwin x86_64) is best effort: topopt was tested on Linux only, the bundle uses the older pins of requirements-macos-x86_64.lock there, the solver auto gives amg, and the time estimate is not calibrated.
